item.title: Report: Dre Greenlaw will appeal his one-game suspension
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: As of now, 49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw is not eligible to play in San Francisco's Week 6 game against Washington on Monday night.
item.content:encoded:
As of now, 49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw is not eligible to play in San Francisco's Week 6 game against Washington on Monday night.

Greenlaw hopes to change that.

Per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, Greenlaw is appealing his one-game suspension that was handed down on Monday after the linebacker headbutted Seattle's Ernest Jones on the sideline during Sunday's game.

Greenlaw was ejected from the contest for his actions.

This is Greenlaw's second one-game suspension in as many seasons, as he was given one last year for unsportsmanlike conduct.

Greenlaw's appeal is slated to be heard by one of the NFL and NFLPA's jointly appointed officers: Derrick Brooks, Jordy Nelson, Ron Rivera, or James Thrash.

item.title: Jags' DaVon Hamilton on filling it at long snapper: "You've got to do a job? Get it done"
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: When Jaguars long snapper Ross Matiscik got hurt on his first snap on Sunday in London, nose tackle DaVon Hamilton filled in.
item.content:encoded:
When Jaguars long snapper Ross Matiscik got hurt on his first snap on Sunday in London, nose tackle DaVon Hamilton filled in. Considering that Hamilton had never done it in a game before, and had rarely even practiced, he did it pretty well, including on the game-winning field goal as time expired.

Hamilton knew all eyes were on him on the last play of the game, but he said he felt fine.

"I wasn't that nervous. It is what it is. You've got to do a job? Get it done. It worked out," Hamilton said.

Hamilton said punter and holder Logan Cooke and kicker Cam Little were both supportive, even after a bad snap led to a missed extra point.

"They were so proud. Stepping up for your team and helping them win games like this, it's a big moment. Whatever I can do, I'll do it to help our team win games," Hamilton said.

Hamilton said he doesn't want to keep the long snapping job.

"No, I'm fine," Hamilton said. "Hopefully I don't have to do it next week and we can move on. But it was fun."

item.title: Report: Steelers WR Roman Wilson is expected to miss time with finger injury
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Steelers wide receiver Roman Wilson had to leave Sunday's win over the Colts with a finger injury and it looks like he won't be making an immediate return to action.
item.content:encoded:
Steelers wide receiver Roman Wilson had to leave Sunday's win over the Colts with a finger injury and it looks like he won't be making an immediate return to action.

Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reports that Wilson is expected to miss a couple of weeks as a result of the injury. He is planning to solicit other medical opinions before any final course of action is determined.

Wilson did not have a catch before leaving Sunday's game. He has 14 catches for 188 yards and two touchdowns on the season.

The Steelers are also without Michael Pittman and Ben Skowronek left Sunday's game with a calf injury. DK Metcalf, Germie Bernard, Brandon Smith, and Kaden Wetjen are the other wideouts on Pittsburgh's roster.

item.title: Quinshon Judkins day-to-day with ankle injury
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Browns could have running back Quinshon Judkins in the lineup for their Week 6 game against the Ravens.
item.content:encoded:
The Browns could have running back Quinshon Judkins in the lineup for their Week 6 game against the Ravens.

Judkins injured his ankle in Sunday's 17-12 loss to the Jets and was seen in a walking boot after the game, but head coach Todd Monken told reporters at a Monday press conference that he is considered day-to-day. Monken also confirmed that is the case for linebacker Carson Schwesinger, who also wore a boot out of MetLife Stadium.

Judkins continued a sluggish start to the season with 14 carries for 44 yards against the Jets. He is averaging just three yards per carry so far this season.

Wednesday will bring the first Browns practice of the week and that will provide the first update on the condition of both players as the Browns move toward their divisional date in Week 6.

item.title: Dre Greenlaw suspended for one game
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: The NFL announced on Monday that Greenlaw has been suspended after he headbutted Ernest Jones during Sunday's game.
item.content:encoded:
49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw has been suspended for one game after his actions during the first half of Sunday’s game against the Seahawks, the NFL announced on Monday.

While he can appeal the suspension, he currently will be eligible to return to San Francisco’s active roster on Tuesday, Oct. 20, as the 49ers play the Commanders on Monday night in Week 6.

While on Seattle’s sideline after a play, Greenlaw used his helmet to headbutt linebacker Ernest Jones, who was not wearing a helmet. The NFL’s announcement notes this was a violation of Rule 12, Section 3, Article 1, which applies to “any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship.”

Greenlaw was ejected from the game.

Greenlaw was previously suspended one game in 2025 for unsportsmanlike conduct.

If Greenlaw appeals, his suspension would be heard and decided upon by the NFL and NFLPA’s jointly appointed hearing officers: Derrick Brooks, Jordy Nelson, Ron Rivera, or James Thrash.

item.title: Report: Micah Parsons is not expected to practice this week
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Parsons is eligible to be activated from the PUP list at any time.
item.content:encoded:
When the NFL announced this year's schedule this spring, there was hope that Packers defensive end Micah Parsons would be back in time to face his former team in Week 6 but it doesn't look like that will happen.

Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that Parsons is not expected to return to practice this week. That would leave him out for Green Bay's Sunday night trip to Dallas to face the Cowboys.

Parsons said over the summer that this week was the "most optimistic" date for him to return from last season's torn ACL. A more recent report indicated that a November return to game action was now seen as the most realistic time for Parsons to get back into the lineup, but Schefter reports that the Packers still hope Parsons will be back before the end of this month.

The Packers have won their last two games to improve their record to 3-2 and getting Parsons back would be a shot in the arm to the rest of their push to advance to the postseason.

item.content:encoded:
The Panthers are getting a couple of players back on the practice field this week.

Head coach Dave Canales told reporters in his Monday press conference that offensive tackle Taylor Moton and defensive lineman Turk Wharton will have their 21-day practice windows opened this week.

Moton is on the non-football illness list due to blood clots while Wharton is on the physically unable to perform list due to a back injury.

The Panthers are thin on the offensive line, particularly as rookie offensive tackle Monroe Freeling deals with a knee injury.

Additionally, Canales said linebacker Jaelan Phillips has a chance to play against the Eagles on Sunday as he deals with a hamstring injury.

item.title: Nick Sirianni's mistake was confirmed by his kick-coverage unit
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Eagles coach Nick Sirianni took the blame for the failure to put the final kickoff of Sunday's London game against the Jaguars into the end zone.
item.content:encoded:
Eagles coach Nick Sirianni took the blame for the failure to put the final kickoff of Sunday's London game against the Jaguars into the end zone. And, yes, it would have made sense to put the Jaguars on their own 35 with no timeouts and eight seconds to play.

The other part of Sirianni's admission is that he knew he shouldn't have trusted his kick-coverage unit to make a tackle. Indeed, the game started with a 90-yard kickoff return for a touchdown by the Jaguars that was nullified by offsetting penalties.

As former Steelers coach (and possibly future NFL coach) Mike Tomlin said during Sunday night's coverage of Ravens-Falcons, a coach needs to be able to trust the players on the back end of the roster to perform on special teams. Sirianni's certainty that he should have called for a kickoff into the end zone contains an implicit concession that he shouldn't have trusted his kick-coverage unit to deliver in that moment.

Which raises a real question about the overall quality of the roster. Do they have enough players who can be relied upon to make a tackle on an important special-teams play? Based on what happened on Sunday, they don't.

Complicating matters is the fact that they apparently plan to devote one of their 53 roster spots, for the rest of the season, to retired right tackle Lane Johnson as part of a strategy to defer the bulk of his cap charges in 2028. That makes it harder, not easier, to have enough competent players to make the play that wasn't made on Sunday.

Which brings it all back to the kickoff decision. Sirianni is convinced he made the wrong call. And the outcome proves his point.

item.title: Report: Lions WR Tom Kennedy is expected to have season-ending MCL surgery
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Lions head coach Dan Campbell said after Sunday's win over the Cardinals that wide receiver Tom Kennedy was likely to miss time with a knee injury, but that the hope was that he avoided a long-term injury.
item.content:encoded:
Lions head coach Dan Campbell said after Sunday's win over the Cardinals that wide receiver Tom Kennedy was likely to miss time with a knee injury, but that the hope was that he avoided a long-term injury.

Monday brought less optimistic news about Kennedy's condition. NFL Media reports that further testing showed a significant injury to his MCL. Kennedy is expected to have surgery to repair the injury and he is not expected to return to the field this season.

Kennedy did not catch any passes in the first five weeks of the season, but saw time as punt and kickoff returner in Detroit. He had 18 catches for 231 yards over 35 appearances for the Lions dating back to 2019.

The Lions also had linebacker Devin White go down with an injury on Sunday. He is set to have surgery on his broken forearm.

item.title: Chiefs bring WR Justin Watson back to their practice squad
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Wide receiver Justin Watson is back with the Chiefs.
item.content:encoded:
Wide receiver Justin Watson is back with the Chiefs.

Head coach Andy Reid said at a Monday press conference that the Chiefs have signed Watson to their practice squad. Watson played for the Chiefs from 2022-2024 and moved on to the Texans last season, but he has been a free agent since being released at the end of August.

Watson had 64 catches for 1,064 yards and seven touchdowns in 50 regular season games for Kansas City. He also had nine catches for 120 yards during three postseasons with the team and he helped the Chiefs win a pair of Super Bowls.

The Chiefs saw wideout Tyquan Thornton go down with a dislocated ankle in Week 4 and there was some talk of interest in bringing Tyreek Hill back in the wake of that injury, but the Chiefs have opted for a different reunion as they come out of their bye week.

item.title: David Montgomery, Jalen Pitre considered week-to-week
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: The Texans have a couple of injury concerns coming out of Sunday’s win over the Titans.
item.content:encoded:
The Texans have a couple of injury concerns coming out of Sunday’s win over the Titans.

Head coach DeMeco Ryans told reporters on Monday that both running back David Montgomery (groin) and safety Jalen Pitre (shoulder) are considered week-to-week.

Montgomery has started each of the first five games for Houston this season, rushing for 138 yards on 52 carries with a pair of touchdowns. Second-year back Woody Marks leads the team with 149 yards on 43 carries with two TDs.

Pitre has also started all five games for Houston this season, registering five passes defensed, a fumble recovery and 24 total tackles.

The Texans will be headed across the pond to play the division rival Jaguars in London on Sunday.

item.title: Dan Quinn remains employed for now, somehow
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Most coaches in the NFL either have been fired or will be fired.
item.content:encoded:
Most coaches in the NFL either have been fired or will be fired. Dan Quinn has been fired (by the Falcons) and he undoubtedly will be fired again (by the Commanders).

For now, the Commanders haven't fired him.

Some have suggested that Sunday's colossal blunder seals Quinn's fate at the end of the year. Properly functioning organizations, however, will implement the decision as soon as it's made, if only to begin the process of searching for the next coach. Really, what's the point of prolonging the situation?

In this case specifically, any effort by Quinn to turn a 1-3-1 season into a playoff berth will be complicated by the task of getting the locker room to do anything other than roll their eyes when the time comes to listen to Quinn. The sooner the organization turns the page on the person responsible for the worst ending to a game since the Joe Pisarcik moment in 1978, the sooner the team can move on.

There's a dotted line back to Super Bowl XLIX, Quinn's last game with the Seahawks. While he wasn't there for the aftermath of the fateful decision to throw the ball at the goal line, Pete Carroll dealt with the fumes of costing the Legion of Boom its "dynasty" label for years. Quinn, who has only weeks to work with, will have a very hard time burying this one.

The issue won't go away quickly. It will be the topic of the week in D.C. Quinn will be asked about it again. Quarterback Jayden Daniels will be asked about it again. Offensive coordinator David Blough — who has yet to receive nearly as much blame as he should — will be asked about it. Other players will be asked about it.

Come next Monday, when the Commanders play the 49ers in Santa Clara, it will be a focal point of the ESPN pregame show. It will be mentioned once or twice (or more often) throughout the call of the game.

Can Quinn turn it around? The 2017 Falcons made it to the playoffs, after the 28-3 debacle in Super Bowl LI. But Quinn and the Falcons had an entire offseason with which to process their meltdown. For the Commanders, the next train is already on the tracks.

The bye is looming after next Monday night. Could ownership decide to give Quinn a chance to right the ship in San Francisco? Could an embarrassment next week be the final straw?

The problem is that the ultimate embarrassment has already unfolded. While stranger things have happened, it's hard to imagine Quinn and the Commanders quickly putting this behind them. The process can't even begin until Quinn finds a way to pull the locker room together again.

How can he do that? The players will be grumbling about this one deep into the coming workweek. Or possibly all the way through Monday and into the week off. What can he say to them to get them to understand how and why it happened?

He can continue to take the blame, but there's no honor in acknowledging the obvious. He'll need to find a way to get them to accept the fact that he made a mistake that never should have been made, and to persuade them to believe that the team is in good hands, notwithstanding Sunday's events.

Maybe an "us against the world" approach will emerge. The problem is that, in this case, the world is right. And the only way to make things right in Washington's world will be for the team to deliver the clearest, strongest message of accountability by relieving the person responsible for the situation of his duties.

item.title: Jim Harbaugh: I can't think of a time where I've been more mad at myself
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh is prone to hyperbole.
item.content:encoded:
Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh is prone to hyperbole.

Whether or not he was giving some of that after Sunday's loss to the Broncos is up for interpretation. But Harbaugh did go to extremes when discussing his decision to go for it on fourth-and-1 from the Los Angeles 41 while up 17-10 with 10:33 left in the fourth quarter.

Justin Herbert got stuffed on his run for a turnover on downs. Denver scored a touchdown to tie it, and then two field goals on their next two possessions to win it the game.

"I can't think of a time where I’ve been more mad at myself," Harbaugh said postgame, via Anthony Gharib of ESPN. "This team works so hard, played so valiantly. And yeah, I take 100% accountability for making that decision and turned the momentum of the game. So it was the wrong one, and I got to be right on those.”

Harbaugh added that the Chargers displayed positive characteristics, but the loss is on him for that choice.

“Really right now the only thing I can think of is I screwed that up, that's really the only thing going through my mind," Harbaugh said. "Because the playmaking, the stops, the momentum was in our favor. And yeah, wrong decision. Both of them. When they don't work, that's my accountability.”

The Chargers will go to Kansas City next week, looking to avoid a 0-6 start before their Week 7 bye.

Harbaugh is searching for answers.

“Yeah, I don't know what that message is,” Harbaugh said. “The players just fight their hearts out, play, give it everything they have. That's the only way, that's the best way.”

item.title: Tests confirm Packers DL Javon Hargrave tore his Achilles
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Packers defensive lineman Javon Hargrave's season is over.
item.content:encoded:
Packers defensive lineman Javon Hargrave's season is over.

Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that tests on Monday confirmed the fear that Hargrave tore his Achilles during Sunday's win over the Bears. He'll have surgery and then begin the rehab process with an eye on a return to action in 2027.

Hargrave is the second Packers defender to tear his Achilles in the last two weeks. Linebacker Edgerrin Cooper suffered the same injury in Week 4.

Hargrave had six tackles, two quarterback hits and a pass defensed over the first five weeks of the season. He signed a two-year deal with Green Bay this offseason, so he remains under contract to the team through the 2027 campaign.

item.content:encoded:
Sunday's win over the Raiders was the fourth game that Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown has missed with the ankle injury he suffered in Week 1 and that means he is now eligible to come off of injured reserve and return to action.

Head coach Mike Vrabel was asked at a Monday press conference if he believes that will happen ahead of New England's home date with the Jets in Week 6. Vrabel didn't commit to any course of action in his response.

"There's a chance," Vrabel said, via multiple reporters.

The Patriots had two underwhelming offensive outings without Brown, but they've righted the ship with better performances in wins over the Bills and Raiders the last two weeks. While that won't lessen the desire to see Brown back on the field as soon as possible, it does make the prospect of another game without him less dire than it felt in late September.

Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that Schwesinger has been diagnosed with a Grade 1 ankle sprain. Schwesinger has not been ruled out for Cleveland's Week 6 home date with the Ravens and his availability will be determined over the coming days.

item.title: Cam Ward: I'm not a loser, you've got to go through stuff to get wins
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Cam Ward has been in the league for one full season and five games.
item.content:encoded:
Cam Ward has been in the league for one full season and five games.

To this point, there’s been a lot of losing.

Ward — who has started every game since being selected as No. 1 overall last year — now carries a 3-19 record after Sunday’s 26-3 loss to the Texans. While Tennessee started the game with a field goal, the team failed to score on its last eight possessions.

The results prompted a question at the end of Ward’s postgame press conference: Have you gotten used to losing?

“No, I’m not a loser,” Ward said. “The record may say that we are that right now. But at the end of the day, you’ve got to go through some stuff to try to get wins. And, I mean, we attack this each and every day. But I mean, for that, no.

“If you’re able to look at everybody in our locker room’s track record, we’ve all won games at a high level. And we’re looking forward to doing that in the long run.”

And Ward isn’t shying away from the responsibility that comes with being a No. 1 overall pick and a starting quarterback.

“I just try to continue to do my job,” Ward said. “At the end of the day, I have a lot of stuff to continue to get better at. I think that’s going to put us in positions to win games, the more I can do my job the right way. But everybody in the building knows, it’s going to take all 11 of us on offense to get things how we want it. But I know as far as my job, there’s still a lot of stuff that I need to clean up. I have to continue to motivate my guys the way they need to be motivated. I have to continue to lead my style. And I think if we keep doing that, if we keep on making progress forward, like I know we can, the wins will eventually come.

“I love the criticism. I love everything that comes with the quarterback territory,” Ward added. “At the end of the day, it’s the best position in the world. Stuff goes the right way, you take all the credit. Stuff goes the wrong way, you take all the blame. I know I’m capable at this position. I have the right guys around me to uplift me and myself uplift them. And we’re going to eventually put it together.”

item.title: Nick Sirianni: "I lost us that game"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The NFL's decision to move the touchback from the 30 to the 35 continues to create some crazy end of game situations.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL's decision to move the touchback from the 30 to the 35 continues to create some crazy end of game situations. And some interesting late-game decisions.

Two weeks after the Cowboys made the wrong decision to put the kickoff into the end zone and concede the 35 against the Ravens in Rio, the Eagles made the wrong decision to put the ball in play against the Jaguars in London.

With eight seconds left after a 48-yard field goal put the Eagles ahead 17-16, Eagles coach Nick Sirianni opted to kick the ball into the landing zone.

Jaguars running back Ameer Abdullah caught the ball at the eight and returned it 53 yards in seven seconds. And a 57-yard field goal from Cam Little gave Jacksonville the win.

After the game, Sirianni took the blame for the loss.

"You know, the guys fought so hard, and then I don't make the decision that, you know, that I should make at the end of the game, and I cost us that game, and I put that fully on me," Sirianni told reporters. "At the end of the day, I didn't make the right decision and it cost us the game. You know, and so there's no other way around it. There's nothing really else to say about that. It's just, you know, I didn't do my job good enough in that situation."

Sirianni was asked whether he watched the end of the Ravens-Cowboys game and other games with key decisions to make as to the strategy of the kickoff.

"Yeah, I watched a ton of those," Sirianni said. "I watch a ton of those situations. You know, obviously we had one against Tennessee. I watched a ton of those situations after that Dallas game, and again, just didn't make the right decision in this particular case."

Sirianni said the decision will stick with him the same way late-game mistakes that he made as a player have lingered in his memories.

"It's just like you would feel if you missed a free throw at the end of the game, or if you had a drop," Sirianni said. "I've been in both of those places. And those ones stick with you, and that will stick with me for a long time. All I know is that I'll work my butt off to get better from it. But, yeah, that one will hurt for a long time. I still think about those other things that have, I've lost games for us in the past as far as, you know, when I played."

Here's the key in this case. The Jaguars, unlike the Ravens, didn't have a timeout in their pocket. It would have been much easier for Philly to defend the sidelines in the area of Cam Little's maximum range.

And Sirianni knows it. If nothing else, his mistake provides further guidance to everyone else as to the touchback/no touchback decision in the final seconds of a half or a game.

Here's the obvious lesson: If the team that will be receiving the ball doesn't have a timeout left, put it in the end zone.

item.title: Nico Collins on C.J. Stroud: That dude is hooping
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: The Texans got their first victory of the season on Sunday, beating the moribund Titans, 26-3.
item.content:encoded:
The Texans got their first victory of the season on Sunday, beating the moribund Titans, 26-3.

After the contest, receiver Nico Collins talked up his quarterback, C.J. Stroud, who has been putting up solid performances — despite Houston’s current 1-4 record.

“That dude is hooping,” Collins said, via transcript from the team. “Everything that is happening right now is the work you put in throughout the week. Coming in leading, as he always does.

“We always got his back a thousand percent of the way and it's only right to continue to keep going, continue to be us, and continue to be 1-0.”

Stroud’s first touchdown of the day came on the ground, as he ran it in from 2 yards out midway through the third quarter.

“That man got a little speed on him,” Collins said. "He got in that thing, and I am proud of him. I am happy to see him touch paint, run his feet. He lowered his shoulder, it’s football.”

Stroud later fired a 9-yard touchdown to Jaylin Noel. He ended the day 26-of-34 passing for 261 yards with a TD.

In five games this season, he’s completed 64.3 percent of his throws for 1,402 yards with six touchdowns and no picks.

item.title: Seahawks' second-quarter blunder handed 49ers an easy touchdown
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Thanks to Dan Quinn's colossal clock-mismanagement error, plenty of other mistakes made by NFL coaches from Week 5 weren't as conspicuous as they should have been.
item.content:encoded:
Thanks to Dan Quinn's colossal clock-mismanagement error, plenty of other mistakes made by NFL coaches from Week 5 weren't as conspicuous as they should have been.

One possible blunder requires further consideration.

With 18 seconds left in the second quarter, the Seahawks called a running play. From their own four yard line. Running back George Holani (who had dropped the ball without contact earlier in the half) fumbled, and the 49ers recovered it for a touchdown.

During PFT Live, Simms said the Seahawks should have just taken a knee and ended the half. It was indeed a nonsensical decision, on the surface, to run the ball. It's not as if the Seahawks were going to pop a 96-yard touchdown run. They opened the door to a possible turnover, and the turnover happened.

After the show, I took a closer look at the situation. The Seahawks had exhausted their timeouts as a 49ers' drive in Seattle territory sputtered, forcing a punt with 27 seconds left. The fourth-down play from the Seahawks' 42 resulted in a punt that was touched at the four and downed before entering the end zone.

At that point, the Seahawks had a problem. The 49ers had all three timeouts in hand. If the Seahawks had opted to take a knee, and if the 49ers had used their timeouts, Seattle would have been punting out of their own end zone with roughly 10 seconds left. And even if the clock had expired on the punt, a fair catch would have set the stage for a free kick on an untimed down from the spot of the fair catch, and a potential three points.

So the Seahawks tried to gain some yards and churn some clock. The problem is that Holani fumbled.

The other question is whether the Seahawks should have refrained from calling their own timeouts. If that had happened, however, the 49ers could have allowed the clock to run down to the final seconds, with either a Hail Mary throw or a 60-yard field goal attempt to end the half.

There was no easy way out of the maze, and the ability of the 49ers to put the ball inside the five put the Seahawks in a box.

The easy solution is don't fumble. The more important consideration is whether a guy who dropped the ball earlier in the half should have been trusted to possess the ball so close to his own goal line.

Regardless, that was a big moment that the Seahawks then had to fight to overcome in the second half. And while they did indeed take a 23-21 lead (and later a 26-21 lead), it would have been a lot easier for the Seahawks to win if they hadn't handed the 49ers an easy seven points right before intermission.

item.title: C.J. Stroud on reuniting with Marvin Harrison Jr.: It's perfect for him
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Coach DeMeco Ryans twice declined to answer questions about whether the Texans had completed a trade with the Cardinals for wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr.
item.content:encoded:
Coach DeMeco Ryans twice declined to answer questions about whether the Texans had completed a trade with the Cardinals for wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. The third time, as he was concluding his postgame news conference, Ryans confirmed the trade.

"You guys wanna know, huh?" Ryans said, smiling. "Yes, we traded for Marvin Harrison. See ya."

The move reunites Harrison with quarterback C.J. Stroud, who played with the wide receiver at Ohio State. Harrison played sparingly his freshman season with the Buckeyes but had 77 receptions for 1,263 yards and 14 touchdowns in 2022 with Stroud as his quarterback.

"I think he brings a dynamic playmaker, somebody who runs great routes and can catch pretty much any ball," Stroud said after the Texans' 26-3 win over the Titans. "I'm super excited to get to work with him. I loved him in college. He's probably the hardest worker I've ever been around in my life, and then there's who he is off the field. He's a great dude, a quiet guy, but you definitely feel his presence.

"I'm excited to get him here, get him learning and get him around the other guys. I think it's perfect for him. Fresh starts are good, so I'm excited to have him with us."

Harrison, who was inactive for the Cardinals on Sunday with the trade looming, has five catches for 85 yards and a touchdown this season. The 2024 first-round pick has 108 catches for 1,578 yards and 13 touchdowns in his career.

item.title: Jaylen Warren runs over Colts as Steelers win 34-22
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The running back finished with 101 rushing yards and a TD on 15 carries and six catches for 87 yards and a TD.
item.content:encoded:
Jaylen Warren had an 80-yard touchdown reception and a 50-yard touchdown run, leading the Steelers to a 34-22 win over the Colts on Sunday afternoon.

Warren finished with 101 rushing yards and a touchdown on 15 carries and six catches for 87 yards and a touchdown.

The Steelers are 3-2 and the Colts 2-3.

Aaron Rodgers had his third consecutive three-touchdown game, with Terry Bradshaw the only other quarterback in team history to accomplish that feat. Rodgers threw touchdowns of 80 yards to Warren, 1 yard to Pat Freiermuth and 17 yards to Freiermuth.

Rodgers completed 22 of 31 passes for 235 yards.

Freiermuth had five catches for 44 yards and Germie Bernard six for 80.

The Colts were outgained 352 to 332 yards, but they went only 1-for-3 in the red zone. They kicked Spencer Shrader field goals from the 4, 22 and 10 after stalling.

Indianapolis was 4-of-15 on third down and 3-of-5 on fourth down.

Daniel Jones was 24-of-44 for 267 yards, with Tyler Warren catching seven for 83. Warren also had a 1-yard touchdown run.

Jonathan Taylor rushed for only 45 yards on 15 carries.

item.title: Kyler Murray is looking like Kyler Murray again
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Through a brief appearance in Week 1 and a pair of starts in Week 3 and Week 4, Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray didn't seem much like Kyler Murray.
item.content:encoded:
Through a brief appearance in Week 1 and a pair of starts in Week 3 and Week 4, Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray didn't seem much like Kyler Murray. The offensive rookie of the year version. The two-time Pro Bowler version. The Road Runner version.

On Sunday, "meep meep" made its way to New Orleans.

Murray looked like the Murray of old again. He completed 24 of 30 passes for 229 yards, one touchdown, no interceptions, and a passer rating of 109.6. He added 51 rushing yards on 10 attempts.

Per the Vikings, the performance made Murray the first quarterback in franchise history to throw for 200 or more yards with an 80-percent completion percentage while rushing for 50 or more yards.

The first hint of the offense waking up came last week, after the Dolphins cut the score of the Week 4 game to 12-10 late in the third quarter. Murray engineered the drive that extended the lead to five and then, after a three-and-out, Murray guided the offense toward consuming the rest of the clock.

Indeed, since Miami's touchdown on the next-to-last play of the third quarter, Murray has completed 36 of 43 passes (83.7 percent).

It felt different this week, with Murray playing well from the start of the game to the finish. Even with a couple of significant momentum-shifting miscues, Murray and the Minnesota offense were never rattled. After the Saints returned a Myles Price fumble 87 yards for the game-tying touchdown, the Vikings drove 70 yards in six plays for the go-ahead touchdown. One more scoring drive provided the final margin of 23-13.

Now, the Vikings enter their bye with a chance to get healthy and prepare for games against the Colts, Lions, Bills, Packers, and 49ers in a Sunday night showdown in Mexico City.

item.title: Broncos rally late for 23-17 win, send Chargers to 0-5
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Denver offense didn't show much improvement, but the Broncos got a win.
item.content:encoded:
The Broncos still have plenty of work to do on the offensive side of the ball, but they'll get a chance to do it coming off of a win.

Head coach Sean Payton's decision to take back offensive playcalling responsibilities didn't lead to a clear improvement over previous weeks, but the unit was able to do enough to take advantage of Chargers mistakes in the fourth quarter to pull out a win. The 23-17 win moves them to 3-2 on the season and it leaves the Chargers to wait at least another week for their first win.

The Chargers scored a pair of touchdowns in the third quarter to jump into a 17-10 lead and they had a chance to pin the Broncos deep in their own territory with a punt with around 10 minutes left to play. Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh opted to go for it on fourth-and-1 from his own 41-yard-line, however, and Justin Herbert was stuffed way short on a sneak.

Bo Nix threw a touchdown pass to Courtland Sutton on the ensuing drive and Broncos defensive lineman D.J. Jones forced a Herbert fumble on the ensuing drive. The Broncos opted to kick a field goal after their drive stalled on the 1-yard-line and then added another after safety Brandon Jones picked Herbert off on the next Chargers possession.

Herbert now has nine turnovers on the season and the Chargers helped set up the first Broncos touchdown of the day with another turnover, so it was another chapter in the nightmare that has been unfolding for the team since Week 1. They'll be in Kansas City next Sunday to face a well-rested Chiefs team that's looking to move to 5-0.

The Broncos only had 95 yards of offense in the second half, they went 1-of-12 on third downs and they had no first downs on any of the drives that were not set up by Chargers turnovers, so Payton certainly didn't correct all that was wrong when Davis Webb was sending in the plays. He'll have a short week to try to make progress and a tough defense to work against in Seattle on Thursday night.

item.title: Lions' Tom Kennedy, Devin White will both miss time with injuries suffered Sunday
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The Lions lost linebacker Devin White and receiver/returner Tom Kennedy to injuries on Sunday in Arizona, and both appear likely to miss some time, but not the entire season.
item.content:encoded:
The Lions lost linebacker Devin White and receiver/returner Tom Kennedy to injuries on Sunday in Arizona, and both appear likely to miss some time, but not the entire season.

Lions head coach Dan Campbell didn't have a definitive diagnosis but indicated that he was concerned about both.

"I think Devin's going to need surgery, broken forearm," Campbell said. "It's unfortunate. I hate it because he was doing some good things for us."

Campbell had similar thoughts about Kennedy.

"TK, doesn't look good. As far as anything short-term, we'll know a lot more tomorrow. I think it could be a sprain, somewhere in there, pretty good sprain," Campbell said.

Campbell did indicate that both will be back before the season is over.

"Neither one of them are going to be around for a little bit here. I hate that. Both players have done a good job for us," Campbell said. "I don't think it's going to be a long, long term. We'll miss them for a little bit."

item.title: Sunday Night Football: Ravens come back to beat Falcons in OT, 30-23
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Derrick Henry had 120 yards from scrimmage and a TD in the victory. Michael Penix Jr. had to exit late with a rib injury.
item.content:encoded:
The Ravens were down by eight with two timeouts when they got the ball back with 2:25 on the clock in regulation.

It took them 1:51 to score a touchdown and a two-point conversion to tie the game.

Then they scored again with a Tyler Huntley 1-yard run in overtime, and Kyle Hamilton grabbed an interception to seal a 30-23 victory.

With Lamar Jackson out due to an ankle injury, the Ravens were nevertheless effective on offense, with Tyler Huntley completing 24-of-32 passes for 201 yards with two touchdowns. He also had six carries for 20 yards with the game-winning TD in overtime.

Derrick Henry rushed for 102 yards and caught an 18-yard touchdown to help pace the offense. Justice Hill also had 73 yards on the ground, including a 47-yard run that set up a score.

The Falcons led for much of the game and even had a shot to win at the end of regulation with 40 seconds on the clock and two timeouts. But starting quarterback Michael Penix Jr. took a hard hit to his side as he was sacked with 27 seconds left in regulation and ended up suffering a rib injury.

Tua Tagovailoa played one snap in the fourth quarter after Penix was injured. While Penix tried to come back in, he was clearly holding his side and looked to be in pain.

After Huntley scored in overtime, Tagovailoa came back in to play Atlanta’s final drive. It actually started well with a 20-yard completion to Drake London, who finished the game with seven catches for 118 yards.

But then it all fell apart, as Tagovailoa’s pass on the next snap went right to Baltimore’s Kyle Hamilton for a game-ending interception.

Penix was announced as questionable to return with a rib injury. But with under three minutes left in overtime, he was, for all intents and purposes, out.

Penix finished 19-of-32 for 240 with one touchdown.

Bijan Robinson had 17 carries for 86 yards and caught four passes for 32 yards.

Now at 4-1, the Ravens will be on the road again in Week 6 to play division rival Cleveland.

The 2-3 Falcons will stay at home to play the Bears in Week 6. But they may have to play a backup at quarterback.

item.title: Dre Greenlaw could be facing another suspension
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: NFL will review Sunday's conduct that resulted in an ejection for further discipline.
item.content:encoded:
The 5-0 49ers had to play without linebacker Dre Greenlaw for more than two quarters. Next Monday night against the Commanders, they could be missing him for all four quarters.

Greenlaw's ejection for head-butting Seahawks linebacker Ernest Jones IV (who wasn't wearing a helmet at the time) could result in a suspension.

The NFL will review the situation on Monday for potential discipline. And that discipline could include preventing Greenlaw from playing in Week 6.

The play itself was inherently unsafe. While not the same as the time when then-Browns defensive end Myles Garrett struck still-Steelers quarterback Mason Rudolph with his own helmet, striking someone who isn't wearing a helmet in the head with a helmet should be a bright line, when it comes to discipline.

Then there's Greenlaw's history. He has now been ejected three times. In 2022, Greenlaw was sent to the showers prematurely for an illegal hit on Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert. In 2023, Greenlaw was tossed after a sideline incident that first introduced a national audience to the legend known widely as Big Dom.

Last year, Greenlaw was suspended for one game, as a result of his post-game interactions with referee Brad Allen following a game between the Giants and the Broncos, for whom Greenlaw played in 2025. And, just last week, Greenlaw had some harsh post-game words for Denver coach Sean Payton after a Broncos-49ers game. (Greenlaw was fined for taunting during the game.)

If a suspension will be imposed, it likely will happen on Monday. An expedited appeal would follow.

item.title: Packers LB Zaire Franklin: Luther Burden said he'd make us quit, but he quit Sunday
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Packers blew leads late in losses to the Bears in both the regular season and playoffs last season, which would have provided Green Bay with plenty of motivation for Sunday's game at Lambeau Field all by itself.
item.content:encoded:
The Packers blew leads late in losses to the Bears in both the regular season and playoffs last season, which would have provided Green Bay with plenty of motivation for Sunday's game at Lambeau Field all by itself.

Bears wide receiver Luther Burden gave them a little but more ahead of the game, however. Burden said this week that the Bears wanted to "beat them real bad and make them quit" and his thoughts were noted in the Packers' locker room.

After the Packers rolled to a 31-7 over their NFC North rivals, linebacker Zaire Franklin called out Burden in his postgame comments.

"You got guys that never really made a real play in this league talkin' bout making somebody quit," Franklin said, via Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com. "That's weird. We don't do that. He quit today, by the way. He ain't wanna play anymore."

Burden had six catches for 47 yards in the loss.
